verdict.root_cause: At 08:36:31 an automated platform actor set a cartservice environment variable that points the service at its Redis cart store on a different port than the one previously in effect (recorded prior value unset; the connection string cartservice now logs targets redis-cart:6380) [tr_c79fcc3e7be2]. From roughly 08:39:57 onward cartservice cannot open that connection: every startup attempt to redis-cart:6380 fails and throws an unhandled exception out of the Redis cart-store initialization called from Main, producing at least five connect-fail-crash-restart cycles through 08:42:15 with no successful connection [tr_0972cafc180e]. Because the process dies during initialization it never serves requests and emits no span metrics at all — cartservice's calls_total series is empty in both numerator and denominator for the window [tr_0010aaceab9b]. Callers see immediate rejection: frontend CartService/GetCart and AddItem spans error in 0.2-2.6ms, and checkout's PlaceOrder aborts inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart at the GetCart call, which is why the checkout error surfaces at checkoutservice and frontend without either of them being at fault [tr_a2f3dadb7f03, tr_4ab1a3c62db5, tr_424ff96c2052, tr_e05bd27b0000]. The failing mechanism is the configuration value itself: it names an endpoint that does not accept the connection, and the wrongness of that value is what breaks every cart request.
verdict.reasoning: Three independent signal types converge on cartservice's Redis connection target. Traces place the origin of the error precisely: frontend and checkoutservice spans only carry errors when they contain an errored CartService child, non-cart paths (product catalog, recommendation, ads, flags) are clean, and the checkout tree terminates at the cart step before any payment/currency/accounting call is made — so those downstreams and the 4 unmeasured edges beyond them cannot be the source [tr_a2f3dadb7f03]. cartservice's own logs name the dependency and the endpoint explicitly and show the failure arising in store initialization from Main, not in request handling, which is the signature of a crash loop rather than in-process degradation [tr_0972cafc180e]. The empty metric series for cartservice corroborates that: a partially-degraded service would still register a denominator, so the absence of any call volume is consistent with a process that keeps dying before it serves [tr_0010aaceab9b]. This also explains the trap the cart-bad-image-tag incident describes — a flat-zero cart error rate read as health, when it actually means no traffic was served. The change log supplies the trigger and the timing: a single environment change two minutes before onset, altering the redis port, with no deploy and no flag flip recorded [tr_c79fcc3e7be2]; checkoutservice has no change of its own in the window, removing it as an originating candidate [tr_00b04094cd40]. Sub-millisecond error spans and the absence of any long-running span rule out latency or saturation [tr_a2f3dadb7f03], and the checkoutservice logs show a healthy end-to-end path at 08:29 that stops completing by 08:38-08:41, matching the onset [tr_e05bd27b0000]. I classify this bad_config rather than bad_deploy because no artifact changed — the running image is the intended one and it would start fine against a correct address; the wrong value is itself the mechanism. Reverting the environment variable to the working port (or otherwise pointing cartservice at the port redis-cart actually listens on) is the fix; a restart alone will only re-enter the crash loop.
open_questions: It was never verified from the Redis side which port redis-cart actually listens on. If Redis was intentionally moved to 6380 and the automation was correcting cartservice, the correct fix is on the Redis/service side, not a revert of the cart variable.

Why platform-automation applied this change, and whether it will re-apply it after a manual revert — the prior value is recorded as unset, suggesting a template or defaulting change upstream that no dispatch examined.
No change query was run against the other five checkoutservice dependencies or against any service outside the 08:29-08:44 window, so a second concurrent change elsewhere is unexcluded.

cartservice log coverage is truncated between 08:29 and ~08:39:57 and stops at 08:42:15; the exact first failure and the state after 08:42 (including whether the crash loop is still running) are unobserved.

Frontend p95/p99 latency and per-dependency breakdowns were never retrieved, so a concurrent secondary degradation on a non-cart path cannot be fully excluded — though all sampled non-cart spans were clean.

The bursty error pattern at frontend (~33% peak) and checkoutservice (~66% peak) with returns to zero is only partly explained by a crash-restart cycle; whether cart briefly served between restarts, or whether some replicas retained the old config, is unsettled.
